runs.name: Hilton Grand Vacations Inc.; NYSE HGV; a timeshare developer, seller, lender and manager; spun off from Hilton in 2017; Diamond bought 2021, Bluegreen 2024; Marriott Vacations and Travel + Leisure read
runs.entry: Price **$35.18** (close 2026-10-13; aggregator quote printed by `tools/run.py`, flagged). Shares **77,724,145**, one class (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-07-30, accession 0001674168-26-000100, cover as of 2026-07-23; `cover_shares.py`; checked against 78,017,947 issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30, shares retired on repurchase, the difference July buying; the 8-K after the 10-Q states no issuance); cap **$2,734M**. Sovereign **5.56%** (US Treasury daily par yield curve, 30-year, 2026-10-13). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (0001674168-26-000017), 10-Q Q2 2026, DEF 14A filed 2026-03-17 (0001140361-26-009850), the 10-Ks FY2019 to FY2024 for the cycle, the 8-Ks since 2025-06; one figure cross-checked (FY2025 operating cash $300M on the filed statement against the tool's 300.0). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7 (the brief's departure), nine stated in the run file; rivals the two named filers, Marriott Vacations Worldwide and Travel + Leisure, 2019 to 2025; Holiday Inn Club Vacations, Westgate and Berkley Group flagged as non-filers, Disney not separable. **Q1 IN**: four businesses the 10-K separates (selling, lending, management, rentals), none technology; the lending arm read under the bank rows as a readable $4.3B book at a weighted 14.7%, funded by non-recourse securitizations, the funding question carried to Q9. **Q2 IN, narrowly**: real estate sales and financing decides at 59% of five-year segment Adjusted EBITDA (the filer's only segment profit measure); for, the Hilton license exclusive to 2051, 74% of sales to existing owners, pre-tax returns of 19% to 33% on net tangible capital; against, real estate margin 28.5% (2019) to 21.2% (2025) while VAC's held at 22.7% to 23.0%, annual defaults 4.1% to 5.1% (2017 to 2019) to 8.6% to 10.8% (2023 to 2025) with credit scores unchanged, the allowance about 14% to 29% of the originated book, members flat since 2022 once Bluegreen is taken out; IN because the position against the rivals broadly held (VPG +9.5% against VAC +6.2%, TNL +38%). **Q3 WEIGHS AGAINST**: the $4.4B of capital added 2019 to 2025 earned about 3.9% pre-tax; organic growth about 1.5% a year. **Q4 no STOP, WEIGHS AGAINST**: ten balance sheets read; Adjusted EBITDA featured, guided and paid on; material weaknesses at 2022-12-31 and 2023-12-31, remediated; inventory about doubled against contract sales, explained; equity $2,151M (2022) to $1,258M (mid-2026) through buybacks, retained earnings $593M (2023) to a $101M deficit, goodwill and intangibles $3.6B from none in 2019, corporate debt $828M (2019) to $4,876M, non-recourse debt $2,896M. **Q5 integrity IN** (Item 1A candid, the allowance raised not released, no restatement); ability weighs against narrowly. **Q6 Part A WEIGHS AGAINST** (the market leg of retention failed, $40.71 at the Diamond close against $35.18; buybacks partly debt-funded, $600M in 2025 against operating cash of $300M; Diamond classed an acquisition by its larger cash part, so the all-stock STOP does not apply), **Part B WEIGHS AGAINST** (pay on Economic Adjusted EBITDA, $1,152M against net income of $99M in 2025, and on contract sales; an independent chair for). Owner cash (operating cash less stock pay and all capital spending plus net non-recourse borrowing, the non-recourse debt treated as the finance arm's working capital, a CONVENTION of the run extending Q7's trade-finance convention) all-equity 64.75 / 489.5 / 504.5 / 641.75 / 727.25 ($M, 2021 to 2025); base **$590.75M** 2022 to 2025 (2021 aberrational, literal window $485.55M beside); maintenance-only $669.25M; purchases $3,110M exceed half of owner cash, so the serial acquirer's organic pair is central at the filer's pro forma 1.46% a year, and the maintenance case inverts (no-growth maintenance-only the top). **Q7 OUT**: value **$94.23 to $95.63** a share all-equity at 5.56% less net debt $4,604M, against **$35.18**; no case earns the floor (best 9.12%, the central pair 8.92% to 9.12%, all spending no growth 8.05%), because $4.6B of corporate debt ranks ahead of an unlevered yield of about 8% to 9%; equity-only returns 15.0% to 17.9% beside; with the non-recourse debt counted in net debt, $18.15 to $32.21 and the fair price negative. Fair **$25.77** all-equity (central), **$60.64** equity-only. Facts after the stop, not weighed: pre-tax interest coverage 1.56 times in 2025 (2.5 in 2023); corporate debt maturities 2028 to 2033, the 2028 term loan B refinanced to 2033 on 2026-07-17; the Timeshare Facility due 2027; securitizations carrying performance triggers; Q12: tour-sold product, 67% financed at a weighted 14.7% under underwriting without income verification, about a tenth of the book defaulting a year, exit companies targeting Diamond owners. Contamination declared by the analyst: a listing of `Test Runs/` filtered for the ticker and name before the first fetch, returning nothing (a blind-rule breach, declared); another company's fold commit subjects in its session preface, not used; `Screens/_daily/` file names only. Commits 9a53627a, b96fe649, 7b315d7a, 2c459b9e, 5e831431, 65a8418f, bd8cc1e9, 183f891d, 73ea25dd (write-early kept, a commit per question; the Q6 verdict line adjusted after the Q7 write-back went in with the close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's check clean (74 ids, 46 fragments); the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` 74 ids, 37 quoted cites, no missing id, no E-id, no slip. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) receivable-secured non-recourse debt has no rule and decides the fair price ($25.77 as the finance arm's working capital, negative if counted in net debt); (2) EBITDA talk still a STOP in Q4's text while the 2026-10-06 convention sends it to Q5 as a weighing, the later followed; (3) specific (a) across two purchases with the organic pair central; (4) Q2's 'ordinary returns' names no capital base, tangible capital used, purchase prices sent to Q3 and Q6, a reading on the other base could close Q2 OUT; (5) the parts convention says operating profit, the filer reports only segment Adjusted EBITDA; (6) organic growth reported as pro forma revenue, chained; (7) the value range at the government rate misleads under leverage, sitting near three times the price while no case earns the floor; (8) the maintenance guess for a developer likely flatters the maintenance case. Could not get: organic owner-cash growth, any segment profit other than Adjusted EBITDA, a guidance-against-results record beyond FY2025, HGV-brand defaults before 2024.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 after Q1 IN (a timeshare seller, lender, manager and renter; the $4.3B loan book read under the bank rows), Q2 IN narrowly (real estate sales and financing at 59% of five-year segment Adjusted EBITDA: the Hilton license to 2051, 74% of sales to existing owners, 19% to 33% pre-tax on net tangible capital, against a real estate margin of 28.5% to 21.2% 2019 to 2025 while Marriott Vacations held, defaults doubled to 8.6% to 10.8% with credit scores unchanged, the allowance 14% to 29% of the book, members flat since 2022 net of Bluegreen), Q3 against (the $4.4B added earned about 3.9% pre-tax), Q4 no STOP with Adjusted EBITDA, two remediated material weaknesses and a buyback-drained balance sheet against, Q5 integrity IN with ability against narrowly, Q6 against on both parts (retention's market leg failed, buybacks partly debt-funded, pay on Economic Adjusted EBITDA and contract sales). Owner cash $590.75M all spending, $669.25M maintenance-only, 2022 to 2025, the non-recourse debt as the finance arm's working capital (a run convention); serial acquirer, organic pair at 1.46%; net debt $4,604M. Value $94.23 to $95.63 against $35.18 at the 5.56% Treasury, no case earning the floor (best 9.12%); fair $25.77 all-equity, $60.64 equity-only, armed. Framework gaps for the operator: receivable-secured non-recourse debt; EBITDA talk in Q4 and Q5; specific (a) across two purchases; Q2's capital base; segment Adjusted EBITDA as the only parts measure; pro forma organic growth; the range misleading under leverage; the developer's maintenance guess.
